speakers.name: Sean Kirby
speakers.title: Detective, Organized Crime Unit
bio: Sean Kirby has been a member of the Winnipeg Police Service for the past 13 years and is currently a Detective assigned to the Organized Crime Unit, where he was a lead investigator and source handler for WPS Project Puma. Prior to his current assignment Sean worked in General patrol, the Community Support Unit, and the Guns and Gangs Unit.
Sean has been with the Organized Crime Unit for the 5 years routinely investigating criminal organizations and involved in a number of successful long-term inter-provincial projects.

Sean is currently a member of the WPS Gang Expert Program, assigned a portfolio in non-traditional organized crime groups. Sean is also a facilitator/instructor in confidential human source handling for the WPS.

speakers.name: Sandra Lloyd
speakers.title: Supervisor and Accredited Team Commander
bio: Sandy Lloyd is a Corporal, Supervisor and Accredited Team Commander with Federal Policing Pacific Region – Drugs and Organized Crime Group 5 (Nanaimo). She has over 25 years of service, 18 of which have been dedicated to Federal Policing. She has been a court-qualified drug expert since 2008. Constable Jason Ebert is also a member of FPPR-DOC, Nanaimo. He has been a member of the RCMP for over 22 years, 17 of which have been with Federal Policing. Their team is responsible for large-scale, Project-based investigations into high-level drug trafficking, and import/export, and Organized Crime groups. In 2024 and 2025, they both expanded their expertise into contraband tobacco when two of their unit’s investigations resulted in the disruption of extensive contraband cigarette distribution networks throughout BC and Alberta. Both have received advanced training from Rothmans Benson & Hedges’ Illicit Trade Prevention Unit on the manufacturing and distribution of contraband cigarettes, and continual training and development in this area. In turn, they have both been recognized within E Division as subject matter experts in contraband tobacco. They have been sharing this knowledge throughout BC and Nationally, presenting in forums including the Canadian Police College Organized Crime Course, Canadian Forum Against Organized Crime and the Counter-Illicit Finance Alliance of BC Symposium.

speakers.name: Lloyd Plomp
speakers.title: Supervisor, Tobacco Enforcement Unit
speakers.org: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission
bio: Twenty-nine year career with Calgary Police Service, spent in Patrol, Drug Undercover Unit, Gangs, CFSEU/ALERT, Targeted Enforcement, Guns and Gangs, Vice, and Agent Handling. Been with Alberta Gaming Liquor Cannabis Commission since 2021 in the Tobacco Enforcement Unit.

agenda.title: The emergence of contraband nicotine in tobacco investigations
agenda.detail: Lloyd Plomp, Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission
agenda.abstract: The growing trend of contraband nicotine in tobacco investigations, and its growth outside of tobacco. A new approach to contraband, and working with numerous partners to combat this new illegal market.

agenda.title: Combatting the distribution of contraband tobacco
agenda.detail: Sandra Lloyd, RCMP Federal Policing Pacific Region
agenda.abstract: An overview of the current landscape and emerging trends in the distribution of contraband tobacco in Western Canada, with a focus on how the commodity is exploited by organized crime groups. The session will help investigators identify contraband tobacco and understand the police powers available to combat a growing trend. Two recent case studies on the distribution of contraband cigarettes and their links to outlaw motorcycle gangs will be highlighted.

agenda.title: Project Puma: a case study
agenda.abstract: A case study of Project Puma. The criminal organizations investigated within Manitoba and their links to the Hells Angels, the Wolfpack and Asian organized crime; the illicit tobacco and the individuals linked to Project Puma; and the file management and disclosure system used during the investigation.

speakers.name: Sean Kirby
speakers.title: Détective, unité du crime organisé
bio: Sean Kirby est membre du Service de police de Winnipeg depuis 13 ans. Il est actuellement détective à l'unité du crime organisé, où il a été enquêteur principal et responsable de sources pour le projet Puma du SPW. Avant cette affectation, il a travaillé à la patrouille générale, à l'unité de soutien communautaire et à l'unité des armes et des gangs.
Il est à l'unité du crime organisé depuis cinq ans, où il enquête régulièrement sur des organisations criminelles et a pris part à plusieurs projets interprovinciaux de longue haleine menés à bien.

Il fait partie du programme d'experts en gangs du SPW, avec un portefeuille consacré aux groupes du crime organisé non traditionnels. Il est également formateur en gestion de sources humaines confidentielles pour le SPW.

speakers.name: Lloyd Plomp
speakers.title: Superviseur, unité d'application de la loi sur le tabac
speakers.org: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission
bio: Lloyd Plomp a fait carrière pendant vingt-neuf ans au Service de police de Calgary, en patrouille, à l'unité antidrogue d'infiltration, aux gangs, au CFSEU et à l'ALERT, à l'application ciblée, aux armes et gangs, aux mœurs et à la gestion d'agents sources.
Il est à l'Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission depuis 2021, au sein de l'unité d'application de la loi sur le tabac.

agenda.title: L'émergence de la nicotine de contrebande dans les enquêtes sur le tabac
agenda.detail: Lloyd Plomp, Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission
agenda.abstract: La tendance croissante de la nicotine de contrebande dans les enquêtes sur le tabac et son expansion au-delà du tabac. Une nouvelle approche de la contrebande et la collaboration avec de nombreux partenaires pour contrer ce nouveau marché illégal.

agenda.title: Lutter contre la distribution du tabac de contrebande
agenda.detail: Sandra Lloyd, Police fédérale de la GRC, région du Pacifique
agenda.abstract: Un portrait de la situation actuelle et des tendances émergentes dans la distribution du tabac de contrebande dans l'Ouest canadien, et de la façon dont les groupes du crime organisé exploitent ce produit. La séance aidera les enquêteurs à reconnaître le tabac de contrebande et à connaître les pouvoirs policiers dont ils disposent pour contrer cette tendance croissante. Deux études de cas récentes sur la distribution de cigarettes de contrebande et ses liens avec les bandes de motards criminalisées seront présentées.

agenda.title: Projet Puma : étude de cas
agenda.detail: Sean Kirby, Service de police de Winnipeg
agenda.abstract: Une étude de cas du projet Puma. Les organisations criminelles visées par l'enquête au Manitoba et leurs liens avec les Hells Angels, le Wolfpack et le crime organisé asiatique; le tabac illicite et les individus liés au projet Puma; ainsi que le système de gestion des dossiers et de divulgation utilisé pendant l'enquête.
